question: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg increases diuresis because:

options.opb: Decreases the peritubular reabsorption of water.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "increased glomerular filtration rate" -> "increased diuresis" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "decreased peritubular reabsorption of water" -> "increased diuresis" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "contraction of efferent arteriole" -> "increased glomerular filtration pressure" -> "increased diuresis" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "increased renal blood flow" -> "increased glomerular filtration rate" -> "increased diuresis" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Increased blood pressure" -> "contraction of afferent arteriole" -> "possible decrease in glomerular filtration rate" -> "unclear effect on diuresis" -> 40%
analysis: An increase in blood pressure typically leads to an increase in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) due to increased renal perfusion pressure. This results in increased diuresis. The most direct mechanism for increased diuresis in response to elevated blood pressure is the increase in GFR, which is often exponential due to the autoregulatory mechanisms of the kidney. This is primarily because the kidneys can adjust the diameter of the afferent and efferent arterioles to maintain a relatively constant GFR over a range of blood pressures. However, when blood pressure increases significantly, the GFR can increase more than proportionally, leading to increased urine output.
